svg.text: monoruby Generational GC — Write Barrier & Remembered Set
The same object graph, marked three ways
A. No generational GC (full mark — same as a major GC)
Every edge is traced from the roots; every live object is marked.
Mark cost ∝ all live objects — a large old generation makes every GC slow.
B. Minor GC without a remembered set — the old→young edge is missed
Old objects (O1, O2) are seed-marked and never scanned, so nothing ever reaches Y1.
Old objects are skipped, so old→young edges must be recorded outside the GC —
that is the job of the write barrier and the remembered set.
C. Minor GC with write barrier + remembered set (monoruby)
The barrier records old→young stores as they happen; minor GC marks from roots + remembered set.
① The store o1.f = y1 fires the barrier → O1 enters the remembered set (armed → remembered)
③ Minor GC scans only the children of each remembered old (mark_children) → Y1 is marked
Minor GC roots = root set + remembered set. Old objects are never scanned, yet old→young edges are covered.
Which stores need a write barrier?
roots are re-enumerated on every GC
young objects are fully scanned on every GC
must be recorded in the remembered set, or panel B happens
old → old: not needed in principle
fires on any armed-old store; harmless over-approximation
